data.narrative:
Astroscale, a publicly traded space and aerospace company founded by Mitsunobu Okada, is currently valued at $840M following $400M+ in total capital raised. Valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 4 same-sector, same-stage public comparables: SpaceX ($1.6T), Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. The 4-company median valuation across this Space & Aerospace public peer set is $23.8B, with a range spanning $2.9B at the low end (Firefly) to $1.6T at the high end (SpaceX). A public-comp anchoring approach using P/S multiples (sector median 24.6x across 6 tickers including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, and SATL) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures for the target.

The triangulated range supports a valuation band of $20.2B to $27.3B, centered on the $23.8B peer median. This implies Astroscale's current $840M valuation lies substantially below the comparable universe, though the extreme width of the peer range ($2.9B to $1.6T) reflects material heterogeneity in the space sector. Key uncertainties include revenue visibility, near-term path to cash flow, and whether comparables' growth trajectories and market positions justify the wide valuation dispersion observed.
